text: Section 36.1 distinguishes three things 'time is unreal' might mean: (C1) objective temporal passage is unreal; (C2) the A-series is incoherent; (C3) time altogether — including earlier/later B-series relations — is unreal. Which claim does the special-relativistic block universe most directly support?
choices: C3, because relativity shows that even earlier-and-later relations among events are illusory
C1, because a temporally ordered world can exist with no frame-independent 'present' and no moving A-series
C2, because the relativity of simultaneity reproduces McTaggart's incoherence regress
None of them, since the block universe is neutral among the three and bears only on quantum gravity
explanation: The block universe abolishes a frame-independent present, so there is no objective A-series passage — precisely C1 — while retaining B-series (earlier/later) ordering. It does not establish C3 (temporal relations survive within the block) and does not reproduce McTaggart's a priori incoherence regress (C2). It is quantum gravity, not special relativity, that pushes toward C3.
